newsitem.title: USA: Sales, losses grow at online bookseller Amazon.com.
newsitem.headline: Sales, losses grow at online bookseller Amazon.com.

text.p: Sales continued to soar in the latest quarter at online bookseller Amazon.com Inc. but losses deepened, the company said late Thursday in its first earnings report since going public in May.

The Seattle-based Internet start-up said it lost $6.7 million, or 28 cents per share, in the second quarter ended June 30, compared with a net loss of $767,000, or 3 cents per share, in the year-earlier period.
Sales soared to $27.9 million from just $2.2 million a year earlier and were up 74 percent over the $16.0 million for the first quarter ended March 31.

Amazon.com raised more than $50 million in its initial public offering and has been spending the proceeds aggressively, announcing online marketing agreements this week with America Online Inc., Excite Inc. and Yahoo! Inc..

As a result, Amazon.com's stock, which had faded after the initial excitement of the offering, has come roaring back, rising $2.875 to close at a record $30.75 Thursday ahead of the earnings announcement.
The results were slightly better than expected. Analysts on average expected the company to post a loss of 32 cents a share, according to the First Call service.
